title: High-resolution Spectroscopy Of $^{162}\mathrm{Dy}$ Rydberg Levels
authors: G. Ferioli, P. Lombardi, P. Sekhar, E. Solé Cardona, N. Preti, C. Drevon, N. Antolini, L. Tanzi, G. Modugno, C. Gabbanini, F. Robicheaux, And A. Fioretti
abstract:
Author(s): G. Ferioli, P. Lombardi, P. Sekhar, E. Solé Cardona, N. Preti, C. Drevon, N. Antolini, L. Tanzi, G. Modugno, C. Gabbanini, F. Robicheaux, and A. Fioretti

The authors report on the high-resolution spectroscopy of over 700 Rydberg states in
[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062807] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: High-resolution spectroscopy of Rydberg states in dysprosium using two-color trap depletion spectroscopy and multichannel quantum defect theory.
motivation: To characterize Rydberg states in dysprosium for potential applications in quantum simulation and sensing.
method: Two-color trap depletion spectroscopy in a magneto-optical trap combined with multichannel quantum defect theory analysis.
result: Over 700 Rydberg states were measured and assigned, with six perturbing states identified.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed spectroscopic map of dysprosium Rydberg levels, useful for future quantum experiments.

title: Nonadiabatic Phonon Renormalization In Metallic Versus Insulating Rutile Oxides
authors: Reshma Kumawat, Shubham Farswan, Simranjeet Kaur, And Kaushik Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Reshma Kumawat, Shubham Farswan, Simranjeet Kaur, and Kaushik Sen

We present a comparative Raman scattering study of metallic rutile oxides ([MATH] and [MATH]) and insulating rutiles ([MATH] and [MATH]). Temperature-dependent Raman spectra reveal that metallic compounds exh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214320] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A comparative Raman scattering study of phonon renormalization in metallic vs insulating rutile oxides.
motivation: To understand how electronic conductivity affects phonon behavior in rutile oxides, which is relevant to condensed matter physics.
method: Temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy on metallic (RuO2, IrO2) and insulating (TiO2, GeO2) rutile oxides.
result: Metallic compounds exhibit anomalous phonon softening and broadening due to electron-phonon coupling, while insulators show conventional anharmonic behavior.
conclusion: Nonadiabatic effects from electron-phonon coupling dominate phonon renormalization in metallic rutiles, distinguishing them from insulators.

title: Chemical Tuning Of Magnetic Ordering And Cryogenic Magnetocaloric Response In Zircon-type ${\mathrm{Gd}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Er}}_{x}{\mathrm{VO}}_{4}$
authors: Ming Zeng, Muqing Su, Liang Ming, Xiaolong Yang, Wang Chen, Lingwei Li, And Hai-Feng Li
abstract:
Author(s): Ming Zeng, Muqing Su, Liang Ming, Xiaolong Yang, Wang Chen, Lingwei Li, and Hai-Feng Li

Chemical substitution offers an effective route to tune magnetic ordering and magnetocaloric performance in rare-earth (RE) oxides for cryogenic refrigeration. Here, we investigate the structural evolution, magnetic properties, and magnetocaloric effect of polycrystalline zircon-type ${}_…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214448] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chemical tuning of magnetic ordering and magnetocaloric effect in Gd1-xErxVO4 for cryogenic refrigeration.
motivation: To explore how chemical substitution in rare-earth oxides can optimize magnetic ordering and magnetocaloric performance for cryogenic cooling applications.
method: Polycrystalline samples of Gd1-xErxVO4 were synthesized and characterized by structural, magnetic, and heat capacity measurements to determine magnetic phase transitions and magnetocaloric effect.
result: Chemical substitution of Er for Gd tunes the magnetic ordering temperature and enhances the magnetocaloric response, with optimal performance at intermediate compositions.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that chemical substitution is an effective strategy to tailor magnetocaloric properties in zircon-type rare-earth vanadates for cryogenic refrigeration.

title: Anatomy Of The Modern Theory Of Orbital Magnetism From First Principles: Term-by-term Analysis In The Gauge-covariant Formalism
authors: Hojun Lee, Insu Baek, Mirco Sastges, Yuriy Mokrousov, Hyun-Woo Lee, And Dongwook Go
abstract:
Author(s): Hojun Lee, Insu Baek, Mirco Sastges, Yuriy Mokrousov, Hyun-Woo Lee, and Dongwook Go

We present an in-depth analysis of the orbital magnetism by means of the so-called modern theory based on the Berry phase across distinct classes of materials-[MATH] transition-metals, [MATH] metals, and transition metal dichalcogenides—highlighting the importance of the microscopic nature of band struct…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214449] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles analysis of orbital magnetism using Berry phase formalism across various materials.
motivation: To provide a detailed term-by-term understanding of orbital magnetization in different material classes.
method: Gauge-covariant formalism and Berry phase calculations applied to transition metals, metals, and transition metal dichalcogenides.
result: Identified contributions from different band structure features to orbital magnetization.
conclusion: The modern theory of orbital magnetism can be decomposed into physically interpretable terms, aiding material-specific predictions.

title: Structural And Magnetic Properties Of Epitaxially Strained (001)- And (111)-oriented ${\mathrm{Pb}}_{2}{\mathrm{CoTeO}}_{6}$ From First-principles
authors: Md Kamal Hossain And Elizabeth A. Nowadnick
abstract:
Author(s): Md Kamal Hossain and Elizabeth A. Nowadnick

The application of epitaxial strain to perovskite thin films has emerged as a powerful tool for tuning their properties, with differences observed between (001)- and (111)-oriented films. Although these effects have been extensively studied in [MATH] perovskites, the influence of strai…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224109] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of structural and magnetic properties of Pb2CoTeO6 under epitaxial strain.
motivation: To understand how epitaxial strain and film orientation affect the properties of double perovskite Pb2CoTeO6.
method: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations for (001)- and (111)-oriented films under various strain conditions.
result: Strain and orientation significantly alter structural distortions and magnetic ordering, with potential for tuning multiferroic behavior.
conclusion: Epitaxial strain is an effective tool to control magnetic properties in this double perovskite, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Interplay Among Spin, Orbital, And Lattice Degrees Of Freedom In The Magnetocaloric Compound $\mathrm{Ho}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$
authors: Noriki Terada, Simon R. Larsen, Takafumi D. Yamamoto, Daisuke Okuyama, Hironori Nakao, Ginga Kitahara, Shuki Torii, Hiraku Saito, Taro Nakajima, Osamu Sakai, Hiroaki Mamiya, Kensei Terashima, Hiroyuki Takeya, Yoshihiko Takano, And Hideaki Kitazawa
abstract:
Author(s): Noriki Terada, Simon R. Larsen, Takafumi D. Yamamoto, Daisuke Okuyama, Hironori Nakao, Ginga Kitahara, Shuki Torii, Hiraku Saito, Taro Nakajima, Osamu Sakai, Hiroaki Mamiya, Kensei Terashima, Hiroyuki Takeya, Yoshihiko Takano, and Hideaki Kitazawa

We investigated the magnetic ordering, crystal lattice distortion, and spin dynamics in the magnetocaloric material [MATH] using neutron and x-ray diffraction (XRD), along with AC susceptibility measurements. Although [MATH] exhibits a ferromagnetic phas…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224436] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay of spin, orbital, and lattice degrees of freedom in the magnetocaloric compound HoB2 using neutron and x-ray diffraction and AC susceptibility.
motivation: To understand the magnetic ordering and crystal lattice distortion in HoB2, a magnetocaloric material, and to characterize its spin dynamics.
method: Neutron and x-ray diffraction (XRD) and AC susceptibility measurements were performed on HoB2.
result: The material exhibits a ferromagnetic phase with associated lattice distortions; detailed magnetic and structural parameters were determined.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the magnetocaloric properties of HoB2 through its coupled spin-lattice behavior.

title: Magnetic Fluctuations And Anisotropy In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$: A Multi-orbital Study Based On $\mathrm{GGA}+U$ And Rpa
authors: Makoto Shimizu And Youichi Yanase
abstract:
Author(s): Makoto Shimizu and Youichi Yanase

Pressure-induced changes in the magnetic and superconducting properties of a spin-triplet superconductor candidate [MATH] have attracted considerable interest, underscoring the need for microscopic theoretical insight. In this paper, we investigate magnetic fluctuations and their aniso…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235137] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic fluctuations and anisotropy in UTe2 using GGA+U and RPA methods, focusing on pressure-induced changes in superconducting properties.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanism of spin-triplet superconductivity in UTe2 requires detailed knowledge of magnetic fluctuations and their anisotropy under pressure.
method: The authors employ first-principles GGA+U calculations combined with random phase approximation (RPA) to compute magnetic susceptibilities and fluctuation spectra.
result: They find that pressure modifies the magnetic fluctuation spectrum and anisotropy, which correlates with changes in superconducting pairing symmetry.
conclusion: The study provides theoretical insight into the pressure-dependent magnetic properties of UTe2, supporting the spin-triplet pairing scenario.

title: Dynamic Monte Carlo Study Of Rigidity Percolation Using An Event-based Ensemble Approach
authors: Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, And Youjin Deng
abstract:
Author(s): Mingzhong Lu, Yufeng Song, Qiyuan Shi, Ming Li, and Youjin Deng

Rigidity percolation provides an important basis for understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials. While most studies on the triangular lattice have focused on static properties at fixed bond (site) occupation probabilities, the dynamics of the rigidity transition remain l…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064141] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies rigidity percolation dynamics on a triangular lattice using an event-based ensemble Monte Carlo method.
motivation: Understanding the onset of mechanical stability in disordered materials is important, but the dynamics of rigidity transitions have been less studied than static properties.
method: The authors employ an event-based ensemble approach to simulate the dynamic Monte Carlo process of rigidity percolation on a triangular lattice.
result: They characterize the dynamic rigidity transition and extract critical exponents.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamic aspects of rigidity percolation, but it is purely classical statistical mechanics with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Relations Among Different Inequality Measures In Complex Systems: From Kinetic Exchange To Earthquake Models
authors: Shohini Sen, Suchismita Banerjee, And Bikas K. Chakrabarti
abstract:
Author(s): Shohini Sen, Suchismita Banerjee, and Bikas K. Chakrabarti

We present a numerical study of several inequality measures across two kinetic wealth-exchange models with extreme inequality features (namely the Banerjee model, and the Chakraborti or yard-sale model) and two earthquake simulating models (namely the Chakrabarti-Stinchcombe two-fractal overlap mode…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064308] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies inequality measures in kinetic wealth-exchange and earthquake models, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand inequality distributions in complex systems such as economic models and earthquake simulations.
method: Numerical simulations of the Banerjee and Chakraborti wealth-exchange models and the Chakrabarti-Stinchcombe two-fractal overlap earthquake model.
result: Quantifies inequality measures like Gini coefficient and Kolkata index across these models.
conclusion: The models exhibit extreme inequality features, and the inequality measures show similar behavior across different complex systems.

title: Emergence Of A Fluctuation-driven Cooperative Solidlike Phase In Potts Model Monolayers
authors: Alexander J. Devanny And Laura J. Kaufman
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander J. Devanny and Laura J. Kaufman

Cellular Potts model (CPM) simulations display significant variation in dynamics, structural ordering, and observed phase transitions. Such differences may emerge, at least in part, because CPM simulations are not implemented in a uniform manner, specifically in terms of the definitions of cell peri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064410] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase in Potts model monolayers, focusing on cellular Potts model simulations and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand the variability in dynamics and phase transitions observed in cellular Potts model simulations due to different implementations.
method: The authors analyze the definitions of cell perimeter and area in the Potts model and perform simulations to study structural ordering and phase behavior.
result: They identify a fluctuation-driven cooperative solidlike phase that emerges under certain conditions.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of model implementation details and reveal a new phase in Potts model monolayers.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, and Deok-Sun Lee

The universal prevalence of cooperation is puzzling, as defection typically yields higher payoffs than cooperation, motivating searches for hidden pathways to cooperation. Here we study a game-theoretic model on a lattice structured population in which interaction payoffs are scaled by the minimum o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a game-theoretic model on a lattice, focusing on wealth gradients and phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of cooperation despite the payoff advantage of defection is a classic puzzle in evolutionary game theory.
method: The authors analyze a spatial game where payoffs are scaled by the minimum wealth of interacting agents, using lattice simulations and analytical methods.
result: They find a discontinuous transition in cooperation levels driven by a wealth gradient, revealing a hidden pathway to cooperation.
conclusion: Wealth inequality can paradoxically promote cooperation under certain conditions, offering insights into social dynamics.

title: Spatial Correlations In Susceptible-infected-susceptible Processes On Random Regular Graphs
authors: Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, And Michael Assaf
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Leibenzon, Samuel W. S. Johnson, Ruth E. Baker, and Michael Assaf

In network-based susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) models of infectious disease transmission, infection can only occur between directly connected individuals. This constraint naturally gives rise to spatial correlations between the states of neighboring nodes, as the infection status of connect…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064307] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spatial correlations in SIS epidemic models on random regular graphs using pair approximation and Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding how network structure and spatial correlations affect epidemic spread is important for predicting disease dynamics.
method: The authors derive a pair approximation model for the SIS process on random regular graphs and compare it with Monte Carlo simulations.
result: They find that pair approximation accurately captures the dynamics for large degree but fails for small degree due to strong correlations.
conclusion: Spatial correlations significantly impact the epidemic threshold and prevalence, especially in sparse networks.

title: ChronoCast: A Time-series Paradigm For Molecular Dynamics Simulation Using Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
authors: Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, And Jie Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxing Wang, Zhongwei Zhang, Shuang Lu, Shuyue Shan, Vitaly A. Kuzkin, Anton M. Krivtsov, and Jie Chen

We propose a time-series paradigm named ChronoCast for molecular dynamics simulation using an advanced autoregressive Equivariant Graph Neural Network, which reformulates the conventionally time-consuming integration process into a forecasting task. This reformulation in turn offers a promising solu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065305] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: ChronoCast uses an equivariant graph neural network to forecast molecular dynamics trajectories, replacing traditional integration.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive due to numerical integration; a time-series forecasting approach can accelerate them.
method: An autoregressive equivariant graph neural network is trained to predict future atomic positions from past trajectory data.
result: The method achieves accurate long-term predictions with significant speedup over conventional MD integration.
conclusion: ChronoCast demonstrates that machine learning can effectively surrogate MD simulations, offering a new paradigm for computational chemistry.

title: Propagation Of Coherent Mechanical Waves In Stealth Hyperuniform Materials In The Transparent Regime
authors: Tony Valier-Brasier
abstract:
Author(s): Tony Valier-Brasier

Wave propagation in multiply scattering media is a fundamental and long-standing topic that has undergone renewed interest with the advent of metamaterials. In particular, disorder control is an efficient way to alter wave propagation. Stealth hyperuniform (SHU) media, characterized by the cancellat…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065505] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies coherent mechanical wave propagation in stealth hyperuniform materials, focusing on the transparent regime.
motivation: Understanding wave propagation in disordered media is fundamental and relevant for metamaterial design.
method: Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of wave propagation in stealth hyperuniform elastic media.
result: Stealth hyperuniform materials exhibit a transparent regime for coherent mechanical waves due to suppressed long-range density fluctuations.
conclusion: Stealth hyperuniformity can be used to control wave propagation, with potential applications in acoustics and elasticity.

title: Algebraic To Exponential Decay Of Spatial Correlations In One-dimensional And Confined Hard-core Fluids: A Laplace-pole Analysis
authors: Ana M. Montero And Andrés Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Ana M. Montero and Andrés Santos

We derive the asymptotic behavior of the radial distribution function [MATH] for one-dimensional (1D) hard-rod systems and related quasi-one-dimensional geometries at high packing fractions using Laplace transform techniques and pole analysis. By identifying the poles and residues of the Laplace tra…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064133] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the asymptotic decay of spatial correlations in one-dimensional hard-rod fluids using Laplace transform pole analysis.
motivation: Understanding the decay of correlations in confined hard-core fluids is important for statistical mechanics of fluids and soft matter.
method: The authors use Laplace transform techniques and pole analysis to derive the asymptotic behavior of the radial distribution function at high packing fractions.
result: They show that spatial correlations decay algebraically in strictly 1D systems and exponentially in quasi-1D confined geometries.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting correlation decay in hard-core fluids, relevant to confined fluid systems.

title: Pacemaker-induced Spiral Wave Chimeras On A Sphere Of Delay-coupled Oscillators: Switching Between Different Spiral-phase Kinks
authors: Chol-Ung Choe, Ryong-Son Kim, And Jin-Song Kang
abstract:
Author(s): Chol-Ung Choe, Ryong-Son Kim, and Jin-Song Kang

Two-dimensional systems of nonlocally coupled oscillators exhibit spiral wave chimeras, a phenomenon that has garnered significant attention in nonlinear dynamics. These chimeras are characterized by the simultaneous presence of synchronized spiral regions and desynchronized phase-randomized cores. …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064206] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spiral wave chimeras in a system of delay-coupled oscillators on a sphere, focusing on switching between different spiral-phase kinks.
motivation: Spiral wave chimeras are a fascinating pattern in nonlinear dynamics, and understanding their behavior on curved surfaces like a sphere is of fundamental interest.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of a nonlocally coupled oscillator model on a sphere with time-delayed coupling, analyzing the emergence and switching of spiral-phase kinks.
result: They observe that pacemaker-induced spiral wave chimeras can switch between different spiral-phase kink configurations depending on parameters.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the dynamics of chimera states on curved geometries, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Regime Identification And Control Of Extremes In The Nonautonomous Lorenz Model With Chaos And Intransitivity
authors: Moyan Liu, Qin Huang, And Upmanu Lall
abstract:
Author(s): Moyan Liu, Qin Huang, and Upmanu Lall

Adaptive chaos control has been studied extensively for autonomous systems. For real-world, nonautonomous systems, such as planetary weather, observations of the system state in response to seasonally and diurnally varying forcing are available only at discrete times and locations. We consider a sto…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064207] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies regime identification and control of extremes in a nonautonomous Lorenz model with chaos and intransitivity.
motivation: Real-world nonautonomous systems like planetary weather require adaptive chaos control, but existing methods focus on autonomous systems.
method: The authors consider a stochastic nonautonomous Lorenz model and develop a method for regime identification and control of extreme events.
result: The proposed approach successfully identifies regimes and controls extremes in the nonautonomous Lorenz model.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for adaptive control of extremes in nonautonomous chaotic systems, with potential applications in climate and weather.

title: General Approach For Partitioning And Phase Separation In Macromolecular Coexisting Phases
authors: Vikki Anand Varma And Alberto Scacchi
abstract:
Author(s): Vikki Anand Varma and Alberto Scacchi

Partitioning of (bio)materials in polymeric mixtures is a key phenomenon both in cellular environments, as well as in industrial applications. In cells, macromolecules are distributed among distinct biomolecular phases. The coexistence of polymeric aqueous phases in multicomponent systems has been w…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065414] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies partitioning and phase separation in macromolecular coexisting phases, a topic in soft matter physics.
motivation: Understanding how biomaterials partition among coexisting phases is important for cellular biology and industrial applications.
method: The authors develop a general theoretical approach based on polymer physics to describe partitioning in multicomponent polymeric mixtures.
result: They derive expressions for partition coefficients and phase diagrams for macromolecular systems.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for predicting partitioning behavior in complex polymer mixtures.

title: Resource And Population Dynamics In An Agent-environment Interaction Model
authors: Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, And Fernando Peruani
abstract:
Author(s): Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, and Fernando Peruani

In any ecosystem, the conditions of the environment and the characteristics of the species that inhabit it are entangled, coevolving in space and time. We introduce a model that couples active agents with a dynamic environment, interpreted as a nutrient source. Agents are persistent random walkers t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064406] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A model coupling active agents with a dynamic environment to study resource and population dynamics in ecosystems.
motivation: To understand the coevolution of species and their environment in ecosystems, where conditions and characteristics are entangled.
method: Introduces a model with persistent random walkers (agents) interacting with a dynamic nutrient source, analyzed via simulations.
result: The model reveals emergent population and resource patterns depending on agent mobility and environmental renewal.
conclusion: The coupling between agent behavior and environment dynamics is crucial for ecosystem stability and biodiversity.

title: Ligand-mediated Magnetic Coupling Across Metamagnetic Transitions In ${\mathrm{CrPS}}_{4}$
authors: Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli Dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, And Nicholas B. Brookes
abstract:
Author(s): Giuseppe Buccoliero, Rachel Nickel, Roberto Sant, Marli dos Reis Cantarino, Andrei Rogalev, Nathan J. Yutronkie, Tristan Riccardi, Daniel A. Chaney, Kurt Kummer, Johann Coraux, and Nicholas B. Brookes

Chromium thiophosphate ([MATH]) is a long-known material: A layered semiconducting antiferromagnet. Its recently discovered gate-tunable metamagnetic phase transitions, the remarkable positive and oscillating magnetoresistance as a tunnel barrier, and its Fano-resonance luminescence, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023323] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates ligand-mediated magnetic coupling and metamagnetic transitions in CrPS4, a layered antiferromagnetic semiconductor.
motivation: To understand the microscopic origin of gate-tunable metamagnetic phase transitions and unusual magnetoresistance in CrPS4.
method: Combines X-ray absorption spectroscopy, X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, and density functional theory calculations to probe electronic and magnetic structure.
result: Identifies ligand-mediated superexchange as the dominant coupling mechanism and explains the metamagnetic transitions via competing exchange interactions.
conclusion: The findings provide a microscopic model for the magnetic properties of CrPS4, relevant for spintronic applications.

title: Contrasting Impurity-induced Magnetism And Dynamics In $2H\text{−}{\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Jonas A. Krieger, Igor P. Rusinov, Sourabh Barua, Aris Chatzichristos, Jared Croese, Derek Fujimoto, Stefan Holenstein, Victoria L. Karner, Ryan M. L. Mcfadden, John O. Ticknor, W. Andrew Macfarlane, Robert F. Kiefl, Geetha Balakrishnan, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Stuart S. P. Parkin, And Zaher Salman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas A. Krieger, Igor P. Rusinov, Sourabh Barua, Aris Chatzichristos, Jared Croese, Derek Fujimoto, Stefan Holenstein, Victoria L. Karner, Ryan M. L. McFadden, John O. Ticknor, W. Andrew MacFarlane, Robert F. Kiefl, Geetha Balakrishnan, Evgueni V. Chulkov, Stuart S. P. Parkin, and Zaher Salman

We investigate the behavior of interstitial [MATH] implanted near the surface of [MATH] using [MATH]-detected nuclear magnetic resonance. We find that, unlike the muon, [MATH] does not show any signature of induced magnetism. This result is consist…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023316] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies impurity-induced magnetism and dynamics in 2H-MoTe2 using β-NMR, finding no induced magnetism for Li8, contrasting with muon results.
motivation: To understand the behavior of interstitial impurities in transition metal dichalcogenides and resolve discrepancies between different probe particles.
method: β-detected nuclear magnetic resonance (β-NMR) was used to probe Li8 implanted near the surface of 2H-MoTe2, comparing with muon spin rotation results.
result: Li8 shows no signature of induced magnetism, unlike muons, indicating a strong dependence on the probe particle.
conclusion: The magnetic response of impurities in 2H-MoTe2 is highly sensitive to the specific probe, highlighting the need for careful interpretation of such measurements.

title: Machine-learning-guided Discovery Of Kagome Superconductors ${\mathrm{YRu}}_{3}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{LuRu}}_{3}{\mathrm{B}}_{2}$
authors: Rose Albu Mustaf, Sajilesh K. P., Sanu Mishra, Junze Deng, Yi Jiang, Kaja H. Hiorth, Eeli O. Lamponen, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Päivi Törmä, Miguel A. L. Marques, B. Andrei Bernevig, And Emilia Morosan
abstract:
Author(s): Rose Albu Mustaf, Sajilesh K. P., Sanu Mishra, Junze Deng, Yi Jiang, Kaja H. Hiorth, Eeli O. Lamponen, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Päivi Törmä, Miguel A. L. Marques, B. Andrei Bernevig, and Emilia Morosan

We report the experimental discovery of bulk superconductivity in two kagome lattice compounds, [MATH] and [MATH], which were predicted through machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening combined with first-principles calculati…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023308] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Discovery of two new kagome superconductors via machine-learning-guided high-throughput screening and first-principles calculations.
motivation: To find new superconducting materials in the kagome lattice family, which are of interest for their exotic electronic properties.
method: Machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening combined with first-principles calculations to predict candidate compounds, followed by experimental synthesis and characterization.
result: Bulk superconductivity was discovered in YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, confirming the predictions.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates the power of machine learning in discovering new superconductors, but the paper focuses on materials discovery rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Confinement And Finite-range Effects In A Quasi-two-dimensional Gas Of Fermionic Dimers
authors: Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, And Grigory E. Astrakharchik
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Midei, Jordi Boronat, and Grigory E. Astrakharchik

A study of a gas of fermionic dimers in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry induced by strong harmonic confinement in one direction is presented. Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo calculations are used to quantify the effects of confinement and finite interaction range on the equation of state and density profiles, with the results benchmarked against analytical theories.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022051] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo study of fermionic dimers in a quasi-2D geometry, focusing on confinement and finite-range effects on the equation of state.
motivation: To understand how strong confinement and finite interaction range affect the properties of a gas of fermionic dimers, which is relevant to ultracold atomic physics.
method: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo simulations are used to compute the equation of state and density profiles, benchmarked against analytical theories.
result: Quantifies the effects of confinement and finite range, showing deviations from simple analytical models.
conclusion: The study provides benchmarks for future experiments and theoretical models of quasi-2D fermionic dimers.

title: Revealing Charge Anisotropies In Metal Compounds Via High-purity X-ray Polarimetry
authors: Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, And Ralf Röhlsberger
abstract:
Author(s): Lena Scherthan, Juliusz A. Wolny, Isabelle Faus, Olaf Leupold, Kai S. Schulze, Sebastian Höfer, Robert Loetzsch, Berit Marx-Glowna, Christopher E. Anson, Annie K. Powell, Ingo Uschmann, Hans-Christian Wille, Gerhard G. Paulus, Volker Schünemann, and Ralf Röhlsberger

Linear polarization analysis of hard x-rays is employed to probe electronic anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity. We use polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of [MATH] to determine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023297] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses high-purity X-ray polarimetry to probe charge anisotropies in metal compounds via nuclear forward scattering.
motivation: Understanding electronic anisotropies in metal complexes is important for materials science and chemistry, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors employ polarization-resolved nuclear forward scattering (PR-NFS) of synchrotron radiation at the 14.4 keV nuclear resonance of 57Fe to measure linear polarization of hard X-rays.
result: The technique reveals charge anisotropies in metal-containing complexes with high selectivity.
conclusion: High-purity X-ray polarimetry is a powerful tool for probing electronic structure, but the work is purely in condensed matter characterization without quantum information or thermodynamics relevance.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but they are often fragile and only appear at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a material platform with intrinsic flat bands stable at room temperature.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and perform angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure, revealing flat bands that are robust to temperature.
result: They observe orbital-selective flat bands that persist up to room temperature, providing a tunable platform for studying strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising system for investigating flat-band physics and potentially realizing correlated phases without extreme cooling.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, and Liuyan Zhao

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different ferroic orders and the formation of complex domain walls in a material with a uniform ferro-rotational state.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were applied to Ni3TeO6 to identify and analyze the polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined ferroic properties, which may have implications for fundamental physics and applications.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis of radiative loss mechanisms.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state may clarify their behavior.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical methods to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic state and describe its properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of relaxor ferroelectrics but does not align with the user's research directions.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases and excitations in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the nature of photoinduced hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems and their unique excitations.
method: Ultrafast photoexcitation and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to probe polaronic and phononic excitations.
result: A long-lived hidden phase with distinct polaronic and phononic excitations not present in equilibrium is observed.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can create metastable hidden phases with novel excitations, offering insights into non-equilibrium states of matter.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key mechanisms and applications of radiation forces and torques in both optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The review surveys various theoretical models, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches, to describe internal conversion.
result: The paper summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open questions in the field.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods for internal conversion are needed to advance applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review catalogs constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, and highlights the current status and future prospects of experimental searches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further experimental improvements are needed.

title: Photon Accelerator In Magnetized Electron–ion Plasma
authors: S V Bulanov, S S Bulanov, T Z Esirkepov, G Gregori, G M Grittani, M Lamač, B K Russell, A G R Thomas And P Valenta
abstract: Strong magnetic fields and plasmas are intrinsically linked in both terrestrial laboratory experiments and in space phenomena. One of the most profound consequences of that is the change in relationship between the frequency and the wave number of electromagnetic waves propagating in plasma in the presence of such magnetic fields when compared to the case without these fields. Furthermore, magnetic fields alter electromagnetic wave interaction with relativistic plasma waves, resulting in different outcomes for particle and radiation generation. For a relativistic plasma wave-based photon acceleration this leads to an increased frequency gain and, thus, potentially to higher efficiency. The influence of a magnetic field leads to quantitative and qualitative change in the properties of photon acceleration, amplifying the increase in the electromagnetic wave frequency.
tldr: This paper studies photon acceleration in magnetized electron-ion plasma, focusing on frequency upshifts due to magnetic fields.
motivation: To understand how strong magnetic fields modify electromagnetic wave propagation and photon acceleration in plasma, relevant to laboratory and astrophysical plasmas.
method: Theoretical analysis using relativistic plasma wave models and magnetohydrodynamics to derive frequency shifts and acceleration efficiency.
result: Magnetic fields enhance the frequency gain of photons interacting with relativistic plasma waves, leading to higher efficiency.
conclusion: Magnetic fields can be used to improve photon acceleration, with potential applications in compact radiation sources.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for analyzing LLHH correlators in conformal field theories, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills, and uncovers hidden symmetries.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: Identifies a partially broken higher-dimensional hidden symmetry and extracts the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for defect-channel double-particle operators.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators in the heavy limit.

title: Direct Visualization Of Field-driven Valence Band Modulation In Electrostatically Reconfigured Graphene Devices
authors: Umidakhon Rayimjonova, Chin-Yi Huang, Yi-Cheng Weng, Elin Cartwright, Fredrik O L Johansson, Noemi Vannucchi, Pavel Dudin, Avila Jose, Pei Ding, David Muradas-Belinchón, Henry Nameirakpam, Zhaojun Li, Andreas Lindblad And M Venkata Kamalakar
abstract: Graphene with ultrathin metal-oxide layers has emerged as a scalable platform for integrated electronic, spintronic, and neuromorphic devices. The in-plane electric fields in such devices are typically inferred indirectly from transport measurements, which do not provide microscopic details of the interface potential profile. Here, we use photoemission microscopy to uncover the precise electrostatic landscape of a complete device comprising diverse, heterogeneous ultrathin metal-oxide-covered graphene junctions. Using in operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution, we directly image the real potential profile across an entire graphene device, including regions covered by AlOx and TiOx nanometer-thick overlayers. Tracking the valence band edge under current bias and gate voltage enables quantitative analysis of internal field evolution via a spectroscopic screening factor, revealing an up to more than 50% suppression of the electric field in graphene covered with oxides, in agreement with transport measurements. This demonstrates local reconfiguration of electric fields in graphene for advanced two-dimensional (2D) device engineering and circuitry, while our operando circuit spectroscopy measurements provide a generic means to uncover intricate potential landscapes and carrier redistribution in 2D electronic and spintronic circuits.
tldr: This paper uses photoemission microscopy to directly visualize the electrostatic potential profile in graphene devices with oxide overlayers, revealing field suppression.
motivation: To understand the microscopic electrostatic landscape in graphene devices with metal-oxide layers, which is crucial for device engineering but typically inferred indirectly.
method: In operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution is used to image the valence band edge across the device under bias and gate voltage.
result: The electric field in graphene covered with oxides is suppressed by up to 50%, consistent with transport measurements.
conclusion: Operando circuit spectroscopy provides a generic method to uncover potential landscapes in 2D electronic and spintronic circuits.

title: Total-Lagrangian Vectorial Lattice Boltzmann Method For Finite-strain Hyperelasticity With Curved Boundaries
authors: Xu Chu Jingsen Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-strain hyperelasticity on curved embedded domains poses a geometric challenge for lattice Boltzmann methods. After streaming across an embedded material surface, the missing population is recovered at the physical cut-link point, where the lattice direction, surface normal, and tangential deformation directions are generally distinct. We develop a total-Lagrangian vectorial lattice Boltzmann method that resolves this geometric mismatch for two- and three-dimensional hyperelastic dynamics. The continuum equations are written as a conservative first-order system for material velocity and deformation gradient. Vector-valued populations are chosen so that their moments recover the state and the material-coordinate Piola fluxes, giving D2Q4\(\times\)6 and D3Q6\(\times\)12 schemes from one \(D\)-dimensional construction. Curved boundaries are embedded by a level set and closed link by link through opposite-population moment identities, cut-link interpolation, and local geometric information at the boundary point. The reconstruction is coupled to a compatibility projection that keeps the recovered displacement aligned with the evolved deformation gradient on embedded active-node graphs. The resulting method extends the previous grid-aligned two-dimensional formulation to curved domains and three-dimensional lattices while retaining explicit collide-stream updates on Cartesian grids. Benchmarks in two and three dimensions show agreement with exact finite-strain fields, nonlinear radial boundary-value problems, and finite-element references.
tldr: A lattice Boltzmann method for finite-strain hyperelasticity on curved domains.
motivation: To handle curved boundaries in hyperelastic simulations using lattice Boltzmann methods, which previously were limited to grid-aligned geometries.
method: Develops a total-Lagrangian vectorial lattice Boltzmann scheme with D2Q4×6 and D3Q6×12 stencils, using level sets for boundary embedding and cut-link interpolation for missing populations.
result: The method matches exact finite-strain fields and finite-element references in 2D and 3D benchmarks.
conclusion: The approach extends lattice Boltzmann methods to curved domains for hyperelasticity while retaining explicit collide-stream updates on Cartesian grids.

title: Gauge Invariant Generalizations Of The Proca Equation And The Yang-Mills-Proca Equation
authors: Nikolay Marchuk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Proca equations (1936) are used in quantum field theory to describe vector bosons (spin 1) with a nonzero mass. The Proca equations are not gauge invariant. In contrast to Stueckelberg's approach (1938), this article presents a gauge invariant generalization of the Proca equation by introducing an additional vector field into the Proca equation. The results are extended to the Yang-Mills-Proca equations, leading to equations with non-Abelian gauge symmetry.
tldr: This paper proposes gauge invariant generalizations of the Proca and Yang-Mills-Proca equations by introducing an additional vector field.
motivation: The Proca equation for massive vector bosons lacks gauge invariance, and the authors aim to restore it without resorting to the Stueckelberg mechanism.
method: The authors introduce an extra vector field into the Proca equation to achieve gauge invariance, then extend the construction to non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Proca equations.
result: They obtain gauge invariant equations that reduce to the original Proca and Yang-Mills-Proca equations in a specific gauge.
conclusion: The proposed generalizations provide an alternative gauge invariant formulation for massive vector fields, potentially relevant to quantum field theory.

title: Experimental Investigation Of Surface Passivation Chemistries For Optical Nanotweezers
authors: Maxwell T. Ugwu, Kewei Li, Abayomi Opadele, Theodore Anyika, Justus C. Ndukaife
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanotweezers are actively investigated as a powerful means to reversibly trap and characterize nanoparticles with profound biological and environmental importance. To ensure that these particles can be reversibly trapped and released, surface passivation is essential. To mitigate the issue of fouling, we investigated the antifouling properties of poly(sodium styrene sulphate) (PSS) synthesized using the Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization (ATRP) technique on our previously reported gold-based Interferometric Electrohydrodynamic Tweezers (IET) device. Fluorescence and interferometric scattering (ISCAT) imaging were used to record trapping performance and study the antifouling properties of our passivated nanotweezer device. The results show that PSS exhibits superior anti-fouling performance against polystyrene nanoparticles when compared to 11-mercaptoundecanoic acid (MUA). By comparing the antifouling properties of PSS and zwitterionic poly(methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine) (PMPC) in preventing extracellular vesicle adhesion, we found that both exhibited similar performance. Overall, the ATRP technique is broadly applicable across nanotweezer substrates with appropriately chosen initiators.
tldr: This paper investigates surface passivation chemistries for optical nanotweezers to prevent fouling.
motivation: Nanotweezers are used for trapping nanoparticles, but fouling hinders reversible trapping; surface passivation is needed.
method: The authors tested poly(sodium styrene sulphate) (PSS) synthesized via ATRP on gold-based interferometric electrohydrodynamic tweezers, using fluorescence and iSCAT imaging to evaluate antifouling performance.
result: PSS showed superior antifouling against polystyrene nanoparticles compared to MUA, and similar performance to PMPC against extracellular vesicles.
conclusion: ATRP-based passivation is broadly applicable for nanotweezer substrates to reduce fouling.

title: Optical Two-Centered Charges, Dipoles, And Conveyor-Belt Modes In Bipolar Coordinates
authors: J. Strohaber
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We holographically generate optical modes associated with bipolar-coordinate solutions of the Helmholtz equation. Unlike conventional Gaussian beam families, these modes support multicenter phase discontinuities. We investigate and demonstrate that they support multicentered phase singularities, including optical dipoles and two-centered charge distributions. We further identify a family of conveyor-belt modes whose intensity structure follows an extended trajectory connecting the charge centers. Experimental generation using a spatial light modulator is presented and compared with theoretical predictions. These results establish bipolar-coordinate optical modes as a new class of structured light fields for singular optics, beam shaping, optical manipulation, and the controlled generation of multicentered topological structures.
tldr: This paper presents a new class of structured light fields based on bipolar-coordinate solutions of the Helmholtz equation, featuring multicentered phase singularities and conveyor-belt modes.
motivation: To explore and experimentally generate optical modes with multicentered phase discontinuities beyond conventional Gaussian beams, enabling new capabilities in singular optics and optical manipulation.
method: The authors theoretically derive bipolar-coordinate solutions of the Helmholtz equation, then experimentally generate the modes using a spatial light modulator and compare with theoretical predictions.
result: They demonstrate optical dipoles, two-centered charge distributions, and conveyor-belt modes whose intensity structure connects the charge centers.
conclusion: Bipolar-coordinate optical modes constitute a new class of structured light fields useful for singular optics, beam shaping, and optical manipulation.

title: Poisson Structures Of Deformed $W$-algebras And Classical $W$-algebras
authors: Uhi Rinn Suh Dong Jun Choi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we explain how classical [MATH]-algebras can be obtained as limits of [MATH]-deformed [MATH]-algebras in type [MATH]. To this end, we give a detailed examination of the construction of deformed [MATH]-algebras via Hamiltonian reduction of deformed affine Poisson algebras. We first derive an affine Poisson vertex algebra (PVA) from the Poisson structure of the deformed affine Poisson algebra. This construction identifies a specific set of generators of the deformed [MATH]-algebra with generators of the classical [MATH]-algebra.
tldr: This paper studies Poisson structures of deformed W-algebras and their relation to classical W-algebras via Hamiltonian reduction.
motivation: To understand how classical W-algebras emerge as limits of deformed W-algebras, which is a mathematical question in algebra and representation theory.
method: The authors construct deformed W-algebras via Hamiltonian reduction of deformed affine Poisson algebras and derive an affine Poisson vertex algebra from the Poisson structure.
result: They identify a specific set of generators of the deformed W-algebra with generators of the classical W-algebra.
conclusion: Classical W-algebras can be obtained as limits of deformed W-algebras in type A, providing a connection between these algebraic structures.

title: Nested Active Pointing Control For Interspacecraft Laser Interferometry
authors: Daikang Wei, Christoph Bode, Yihao Yan, Vitali M\"uller, Juan Jos\'e Esteban Delgado, Gerhard Heinzel
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise pointing control is a critical requirement for interspacecraft laser interferometry, as angular misalignment introduces measurement noise and even leads to laser link loss. We present a nested control architecture that uses differential wavefront sensing signals to drive a fast steering mirror (FSM) to track the incoming beam, while feeding the FSM's angular changes back to the attitude and orbit control system (AOCS) to suppress angle-dependent optical path variations. This scheme is experimentally validated in our hexapod-based setup. Relative to standalone FSM actuation, the nested configuration enhanced pointing stability by 6.9 dB and 4.9 dB in the horizontal and vertical directions across the frequency band from 3 mHz to the AOCS actuation's unity-gain frequency. Additionally, tilt-to-length coupling was suppressed by an order of magnitude below 6 mHz and by two orders of magnitude below 0.45 mHz. These results demonstrate the feasibility of nested active pointing control for future interspacecraft laser interferometry missions.
tldr: This paper presents a nested control architecture for interspacecraft laser interferometry, improving pointing stability and reducing tilt-to-length coupling.
motivation: Precise pointing control is critical for interspacecraft laser interferometry to minimize measurement noise and prevent laser link loss.
method: A nested control loop uses differential wavefront sensing to drive a fast steering mirror (FSM) for beam tracking, with FSM angular changes fed back to the attitude and orbit control system (AOCS) to suppress angle-dependent optical path variations.
result: The nested configuration enhanced pointing stability by 6.9 dB and 4.9 dB in horizontal and vertical directions (3 mHz to AOCS unity-gain frequency) and suppressed tilt-to-length coupling by one to two orders of magnitude below 6 mHz.
conclusion: The nested active pointing control scheme is feasible for future interspacecraft laser interferometry missions.

title: MADField: Multi-fidelity Amortized Density Field For Adsorption In Nanoporous Materials
authors: Yoonho Kim, Seongsu Kim, Sungsoo Ahn, Honghui Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-throughput computational screening of nanoporous materials for gas storage and separation requires fast and accurate characterization of adsorption equilibrium. Particle-based grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) and density-based classical density functional theory (cDFT) provide simulation-based estimates of gas uptake and adsorbate density fields, but their speed-accuracy tradeoff remains insufficient for large-scale screening. In this work, we address this gap with Multi-fidelity Amortized Density Field for Adsorption in Nanoporous Materials (MADField), which reframes adsorption prediction as equilibrium density-field estimation. MADField learns from two complementary fidelities, combining broad and scalable cDFT density supervision with higher-fidelity GCMC density labels, and recovers gas uptake by integrating the predicted density field. MADField improves uptake accuracy over the strongest baselines by 6.0x for cDFT and 15.4x for GCMC, and its predicted fields accelerate cDFT solvers with 2.0x fewer iteration steps while recovering 42 percent of cases that fail under standard settings. Finally, we evaluate MADField for conventional CH4 working capacity screening on the 270k-structure ARC-MOF database. Within this space of extremely rare high-capacity targets, 167 in total, the model achieves 56x higher average precision than the strongest baseline and accelerates inference by five orders of magnitude compared to GCMC. By prioritizing the MADField rankings, selecting the top 1.7 percent of candidates recovers 95 percent of all targets, while the top 6 percent ensures 100 percent recall.
tldr: MADField uses multi-fidelity machine learning to predict gas adsorption density fields in nanoporous materials, combining cDFT and GCMC data for faster screening.
motivation: High-throughput screening of nanoporous materials for gas storage requires fast and accurate adsorption predictions, but existing methods (GCMC, cDFT) have a speed-accuracy tradeoff.
method: The model learns from two fidelities: broad cDFT density supervision and higher-fidelity GCMC density labels, predicting equilibrium density fields and integrating them to estimate gas uptake.
result: MADField improves uptake accuracy by 6x over cDFT and 15.4x over GCMC baselines, and in CH4 screening on 270k MOFs, it achieves 56x higher average precision and 100% recall in top 6% of candidates.
conclusion: Multi-fidelity learning effectively accelerates adsorption prediction, enabling large-scale screening of nanoporous materials.

title: A Dressed Polarizability Framework For Interface-coupled Meta-atoms And Large-scale Metasurfaces
authors: Peng Fu, Jean-Paul Hugonin, Maxime Bertrand, Kevin Vynck, P. Lalanne
abstract: ArXiv:2606.21302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modeling of large collections of interacting meta-atoms remains a central challenge in photonics because it requires the simultaneous treatment of complex scatterer geometries, multiple scattering, and heterogeneous environments. Here, we introduce the dressed Global Polarizability Matrix (dGPM), a reduced-order electromagnetic framework in which complex meta-atoms are represented by compact scattering operators that explicitly incorporate the influence of nearby interfaces. The dGPM accurately reconstructs near- and far-field electromagnetic responses for interface-coupled structures, including geometries beyond the practical applicability of conventional T-matrix approaches. The framework naturally combines interface-coupled and free-space scatterers within a unified multiple-scattering formalism and enables simulations of large ordered and disordered metasurfaces. More broadly, the dGPM extends operator-based electromagnetic modeling to heterogeneous photonic environments while preserving a compact scatterer-based representation, providing an efficient framework for the simulation and design of large-scale photonic systems.
tldr: Introduces a dressed global polarizability matrix framework for efficient electromagnetic modeling of large metasurfaces with interface-coupled meta-atoms.
motivation: Modeling large collections of interacting meta-atoms in heterogeneous environments is computationally challenging; existing methods like T-matrix approaches are limited for interface-coupled structures.
method: The dressed Global Polarizability Matrix (dGPM) represents complex meta-atoms as compact scattering operators that incorporate interface effects, enabling unified multiple-scattering simulations.
result: The dGPM accurately reconstructs near- and far-field responses for interface-coupled structures and scales to large ordered and disordered metasurfaces.
conclusion: The framework provides an efficient, compact representation for simulating and designing large-scale photonic systems in heterogeneous environments.

title: A Delayed Generalized Lotka--Volterra Model For Threshold Instability And Structural Recognition
authors: Carlo Cattani
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a delayed generalized Lotka--Volterra model for systems in which structural change and recognition of change are not synchronized. The starting point is the idea that a system may accumulate internal transformations while remaining locally stable at the level of interpretation, governance, or perception. Instability becomes effective only when accumulated structural stress crosses a threshold and is recognized after a delay. We introduce a vector of civilizational state variables including systemic complexity, informational entropy, systemic pressure, resilience, and legitimacy. Their interaction is modeled through a delayed generalized Lotka--Volterra system. The delays represent the temporal separation between structural variation and its cognitive, institutional, or social effects. A composite instability functional is then defined, and threshold crossing is interpreted as the transition from latent instability to recognized instability. The paper studies positivity, equilibria, linearization, and local stability of the delayed system. Particular attention is given to delay-induced instability: even when the corresponding non-delayed system is locally stable, sufficiently large delays may destabilize the equilibrium and generate oscillatory or nonlinear behavior. The model provides a mathematical framework for delayed recognition, threshold instability, and the emergence of crises in complex adaptive systems.
tldr: A delayed Lotka-Volterra model for threshold instability and structural recognition in complex adaptive systems, applied to civilizational state variables.
motivation: To model systems where structural change and recognition are not synchronized, leading to delayed instability and crises.
method: Introduces a delayed generalized Lotka-Volterra system with variables like complexity, entropy, and resilience; analyzes positivity, equilibria, and delay-induced instability.
result: Shows that delays can destabilize otherwise stable equilibria, leading to oscillations or nonlinear behavior.
conclusion: Provides a mathematical framework for understanding delayed recognition and threshold instability in complex systems.

title: The Normalized Orbit Of A Bounded Normal Operator Can Be A Frame
authors: G\"otz E. Pfander Ilya A. Krishtal
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conjecture 3 in [A. Aldroubi, C. Cabrelli, I. Krishtal, and U. Molter, Dynamical Sampling: A Survey, La Matematica 5 (2026), Article 37] postulates that for any bounded normal operator [MATH] on a Hilbert space [MATH] and any vector [MATH] the system \[ \left\{{\|T^k g\|}: k=0,1,2,\ldots\right\} \] is not a frame. It was motivated by [A. Aldroubi, C. Cabrelli, A. F. akmak, U. Molter, and A. Petrosyan, Iterative actions of normal operators, J. Funct. Anal. 272 (2017), no. 3, 1121--1146], where it was established that such frames do not exist when [MATH] is a self adjoint operator. We show, however, that this conjecture is false by presenting a construction of [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] such that the normalized orbit considered is indeed a frame. The operator is diagonal and is defined via a decomposition of the space into finite blocks rapidly increasing in size. We also provide an [MATH]-perturbation [MATH] of the operator [MATH] such that the system \[ \left\{{S^k g}: k=0,1,2,\ldots\right\} \] is a Carleson frame in the sense of [A. Aldroubi, C. Cabrelli, U. Molter, and S. Tang, Dynamical sampling, Appl. Comput. Harmon. Anal. 42 (2017), no. 3, 378--401] and [O. Christensen, M. Hasannasab, F. M. Philipp, and D. Stoeva, The mystery of Carleson frames, Appl. Comput. Harmon. Anal. 72 (2024), Article 101659]. The constructions were achieved using ChatGPT, whose assistance was also employed in the preparation of this manuscript.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture about frames formed by normalized orbits of bounded normal operators, constructing a counterexample using a block-diagonal operator.
motivation: The conjecture that normalized orbits of bounded normal operators cannot form frames was motivated by prior work on self-adjoint operators; the authors aim to show it is false.
method: The authors construct a diagonal operator on a Hilbert space decomposed into finite blocks of rapidly increasing size, and define a vector such that the normalized orbit forms a frame.
result: They provide an explicit counterexample to Conjecture 3, and also construct a perturbation that yields a Carleson frame.
conclusion: The conjecture is false; normalized orbits of bounded normal operators can indeed be frames, contrary to previous expectations.

title: Neural Network Approximation In Discrete Dual Norms With Adaptive Test Spaces
authors: Tanakorn Udomworarat, Ignacio Brevis, Kristoffer G. van der Zee, Sergio Rojas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.20972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In robust variational physics-informed neural networks (RVPINNs), the loss function is formulated in terms of the Riesz representative of the variational residual within a discrete test space. This approach guarantees that the loss function is robust with respect to the true error in the energy norm up to a remainder term that depends on both the neural network approximation and the discrete space configuration. However, in problems with localized singularities, steep gradients, or interface layers, a fixed coarse test space may fail to resolve the continuous Riesz representative of the residual during training. Although this can be avoided by using a sufficiently fine test space from the start, doing so may be computationally inefficient. We therefore propose an adaptive algorithm that enriches the test space only where the error between the discrete and continuous Riesz representatives is pronounced. We establish theoretical adaptive strategies within the RVPINN framework and derive their error bounds. Furthermore, we propose a computable refinement indicator and prove that, under the saturation assumption, it serves as a reliable and efficient error estimator for the non-computable discrepancy between the discrete and continuous Riesz representatives. Finally, we propose a practical adaptive algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness through numerical experiments on elliptic Dirichlet problems.
tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive algorithm for enriching test spaces in robust variational physics-informed neural networks (RVPINNs) to improve approximation in problems with localized features.
motivation: Fixed coarse test spaces in RVPINNs may fail to resolve the continuous Riesz representative of the residual in problems with singularities or steep gradients, while using a fine test space from the start is computationally inefficient.
method: The authors develop an adaptive algorithm that enriches the test space where the error between discrete and continuous Riesz representatives is large, using a computable refinement indicator based on the saturation assumption.
result: The refinement indicator is proven to be a reliable and efficient error estimator for the discrepancy between discrete and continuous Riesz representatives, and numerical experiments on elliptic Dirichlet problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the adaptive algorithm.
conclusion: The adaptive test space enrichment improves the efficiency and accuracy of RVPINNs for problems with localized features, without requiring a uniformly fine test space.

The remaining eight missing weights are necessary to give a positive answer to an open question on the weight spectrum of [MATH] for [MATH].

tldr: The paper develops a non-commutative calculus and Getzler-Gauss-Manin connection for open-closed homotopy algebras, focusing on algebraic structures in homotopy theory.
motivation: To extend the calculus structure and Gauss-Manin connection to the setting of open-closed homotopy algebras, which are important in algebraic topology and mathematical physics.
method: The author establishes a calculus structure on Hochschild invariants and defines a Getzler-Gauss-Manin connection on the open-closed periodic cyclic chain complex, proving flatness up to chain homotopy.
